synopsis: MAE, MAPE and RMSE summarize simulation-versus-measurement differences as average error figures, but they hide the error distribution and are insufficient on their own for complete validation [f14779, f14785, f14789]. On-road lidar mapping with pose refinement reduced map thickness error from 4.5 cm to 1.3 cm MAE; a separate 2022 physical-lidar study reported 14.65 cm mean depth error at 33 m against an Ouster sensor, using indoor and outdoor objects rather than a job site [f3804, f3929]. A ray-traced lidar model achieved MAPE values of 1.7% for amplitude, 8.5% for point count and 9.3% for mean intensity only when the full processing chain and sensor imperfections were modeled; the cited evidence is on-road [f4417, f12605]. Published lidar applications report MAPE rather than use it as a thresholded acceptance criterion, and MAPE misbehaves near zero measured values [f7766, f14783]. Low average error can coexist with dangerous optimism near the collision boundary, while conventional mean and RMSE errors cannot accommodate both aleatory and epistemic uncertainty in stochastic radar detections [f7816, f4821]. The corpus reports that a validated radar or camera dust model with a published error metric was searched for but not found [f254].
